newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts eyeing Siemens for positive signs.
newsitem.headline: Analysts eyeing Siemens for positive signs.

text.p: Analysts will listen closely for signs of a more positive outlook from Siemens AG on Thursday when the German industrial group presents its nine-month results to the financial community.
Siemens on Monday told reporters it stood by an earlier forecast of flat profit in 1996/97 -- even through nine-month net income rose three percent to 1.705 billion marks.
But some analysts said the company might give a more bullish outlook when chief financial officer Karl-Hermann Baumann meets analysts away from the glare of the media.

"I think Baumann might be more positive with the outlook for analysts," said Hans Peter Wodniok at Credit Lyonnais in Frankfurt. "If he is, then you would probably see a positive reaction on the market."
Other analysts doubted whether Siemens would alter its message.
"Siemens doesn't usually do that," said Peter Thilo Hasler at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich. "I wouldn't count on them saying anything different to us."
Siemens shares traded at 118.90 marks at 1100 GMT on Wednesday, up 3.20, or 2.7 percent, as the blue-chip DAX index surged 3.89 percent to 4,394.99.
On Monday, investors were hoping for a new profit forecast based on the strong dollar's positive effect on Siemens exports.
When the company kept to its its flat outlook later that day, its shares fell five marks.
Wodniok said Baumann might also give analysts an update on Siemens move to enterprise value added(EVA), an increasingly popular method of comparing costs to profit to determine a company's returns.
"Baumann may say something about EVA and that would be positive to a lot of analysts," Wodniok said.
Analysts are also due to hear from the company's Public Communications (ON) group, which Baumann said on Monday would be the most profitable in the year ending September 30.

The Automotive Technology (AT) units and its Industrial Drives business (ASI) would also give presentations but analysts doubted whether either was likely to offer a particularly impressive profit outlook.
A Siemens spokesman confirmed that Baumann would host an analyst meeting on Thursday highlighted by presentations by ON, AT and ASI.
In the first nine months of this year, ON's sales rose 28 percent to 9.9 billion marks, while orders surged 26 percent to 13.1 billion. Last year's pretax profit was 354 million marks.
AT had 3.4 billion in sales and the same total in orders, with both showing 13 percent gains. Last year's pretax profit was 111 million marks.

Siemens said on Monday nine-month sales rose 10 percent to 71.2 billion marks and forecast sales of more than 110 billion marks for the year ending September 30, with net income equalling its 1995/96 total of 2.491 billion marks.
